chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Atlanta, the Eighty-One Theatre and Black education
summary: Danny describes Atlanta as the metropolis of the Black South, with the Eighty-One Theatre on the TOBA circuit, insurance companies and colleges.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, there was a junction. There was the Eight-One Theatre. It was a theatre that was one of the pivots of the TOBA Circuit, the Eighty-One Theatre. They had three theatres of vaudeville in Atlanta. And Atlanta was like the metropolis of the Black South, more so than New Orleans. They had three or four big insurance companies there.
They had a whole lot of money there in Atlanta, Georgia...
Well, about six schools. Spellman, and they've got schools...Atlanta University...
Yeah, there's nothin' but schools. It's the height of education for Black people around there.
So there was this market for Black vaudeville. And you played the Eighty-One Theatre, the Crawford... His daddy was
the piano player in that theatre for years -- Eddie Heywood's daddy. [EDDIE HEYWOOD, SR.]
Yeah. I hear he was a pretty good piano player, too.
